candidates.title: Daily hiring alerts for target companies

demandEvidence.chore: Track new hiring postings at target companies and notify the operator when new postings appear.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Sharing a simple pattern I use for tracking hiring at target companies.

experimentPlan.output: A daily digest of newly found public job postings for a supplied list of target companies.
inputs: Synthetic list of target company career-site URLs
Public job posting title, location, and URL returned by an accessible scraper
Operator-defined target list and alert channel
experimentPlan.trigger: Once each morning, check the supplied target-company sources for new public postings.
steps: Run an available public job scraper for each supported source.
Keep only postings returned as new by the scraper.
Format title, location, and URL into a digest.
Show the digest to an operator for review before sharing.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: On a fixed test list, compare a sample run with manually checked public postings and confirm each included item has a title, location, and working source URL.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: The operator must authorize target sources, verify scraper terms and access, check relevance and duplicates, and approve any shared digest.
unverified: Reliable access to each selected career site and scraper is unverified.
The post reports the maker’s workflow; this does not independently verify its current operation, cost, or coverage.
Buyer willingness to pay and repeat demand are unknown.

ease.reason: The described daily trigger, scraper, filter, and alert give a concrete starting pattern, but the required scraper access and setup remain unverified.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small recruiting or consulting teams may value target-company alerts; this post establishes no buying intent or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week alert prototype is bounded, but account access, scraper reliability, costs, and coverage need validation.

autonomy.reason: The described loop filters new postings and sends alerts; a person must choose targets, validate results, and review alerts.

evidence.reason: The retained spans give a specific hiring-tracking workflow and maker-reported operation, but no independent use or recurring buyer evidence.

candidates.reason: The post supports a concrete proposed alert workflow, but the provisional mean is below six because buyer willingness and current scraper operation are unverified.

candidates.title: Prepare resume answers for job forms

demandEvidence.chore: Enter resume information into forms tailored to each company’s hiring process.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: filling my resume data to freshly developed forms made specifically to the hiring process

experimentPlan.output: A review sheet that maps supplied resume facts to draft answers for repeated job-application fields.
inputs: Fictional resume facts supplied by the tester
A small set of manually transcribed sample form field labels
experimentPlan.trigger: When a tester receives another application form with fields represented in the sample set.
steps: Enter fictional resume facts into a structured table.
Add the sample form field labels.
Suggest matching facts for each field.
Flag fields with no clear match instead of guessing.
Have a person review and copy approved answers manually.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: For each sample field, verify the suggested answer matches the corresponding fictional resume fact and leaves uncertain fields blank.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person must provide lawful test inputs, check every answer, handle sensitive information safely, and complete the actual application.
unverified: Actual employer form layouts and field variations are unavailable.
No supplied source supports form reading, browser automation, or automatic submission.
Whether job seekers or career services would pay is unknown.

ease.reason: A student can test extraction into a review table, but the source gives no form fields or supported software reference.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: job seekers or career services might value reducing repeated form entry; this post establishes no payment intent.

feasibility.reason: A draft-only test with fictional resume facts and sample fields is bounded; real employer forms and validation are unavailable.

autonomy.reason: A tool could suggest field values, but a person must verify every answer and submit each application; submission is unsupported.

evidence.reason: The post states repeated resume-data entry into company-specific forms, but gives no form examples, frequency beyond this account, or corroboration.

candidates.reason: The concrete repeated data-entry chore supports a proposed draft-only test, but there is no field-level or implementation evidence and the provisional mean is below six.

candidates.title: Check invoice rows before an API handoff

demandEvidence.chore: Map a variable number of CRM invoice rows into an external system’s HTTP request.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I cannot map array data for dynamic amount of invoice rows to the HTTP POST module’s “invoice rows” section

experimentPlan.output: A draft invoice-row payload from fictional CRM rows, with a visible field-by-field mapping for operator review.
inputs: Fictional CRM record with two or more invoice rows
Operator-supplied field names for a mock invoice request
experimentPlan.trigger: When the operator supplies a fictional CRM record with a variable number of invoice rows.
steps: Represent the fictional line items as an array.
Map each chosen line-item field to a mock request field.
Display the resulting payload without sending it.
Flag missing or mismatched fields for review.
Have an operator compare the draft against the input rows.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: For two fictional rows, verify that both appear in the displayed draft with their supplied values and that no external request is sent.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person must define field mappings, check arithmetic and tax treatment, and authorize any real endpoint use; this proposal does not create or persist invoices.
unverified: The Make reference (e73220ebd327caecbae34a3c) documents array indexing, not invoice APIs or a complete row-mapping workflow.
The named external endpoint and its schema are unavailable.
Invoice persistence and tax correctness are unverified.
Buyer willingness to pay is unknown.

ease.reason: The Make reference (e73220ebd327caecbae34a3c) explains array indexes, useful for a synthetic mapping mock; invoice payload mechanics remain unsupported.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small service firms might pay for invoice preparation help; one troubleshooting post establishes no buyer intent or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week synthetic payload comparison is bounded, but external endpoint behavior, persistence, and tax correctness are unverified.

autonomy.reason: A draft can map supplied rows, but a person must verify totals and authorize any external submission; no execution is documented.

evidence.reason: The retained post gives a specific dynamic invoice-row mapping problem and sample arrays; it does not verify an endpoint, persisted invoice, or tax result.

candidates.reason: A specific chore and the supplied array-indexing reference support a narrow mock, but key invoice mechanics are absent and the provisional mean is below six.
